walkthroughs.body_html: In the UK: barm, cob, bap, roll, bread cake, stottie. The thing's the same — the word varies by region.
Lexical variation is when speakers use different words for the same item — proof that English bends to community.
Regional words carry identity. Calling something a 'cob' marks you Midlands; 'stottie' marks you Geordie. Words anchor home.

Standard English is the same as Received Pronunciation.
Inflectional morphology applies only to verbs and derivational only to nouns.
Standard English is the original and correct form of the language.
A dialect that has gained social and institutional prestige — used in education and formal writing; it is one variety, not inherently superior in linguistic terms.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between inflectional and derivational morphology?
options: Inflectional morphology applies only to verbs and derivational only to nouns.
Inflection and derivation are two words for the same process.

Inflectional morphemes mark grammatical features without changing word class (cat/cats, walk/walked); derivational morphemes create new words, often changing word class (happy → happiness, teach → teacher).
Vygotsky was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
